analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The sole changed line is head line 1406, a new table row documenting `demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens`. The row says the paged complete store's effective-token floor applies to dense Qwen3.5/3.8 and is otherwise unset. When the floor is met, a range ends just below the prompt end. It cites `EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift`, which is not supplied. The remaining text in both units is unchanged context and was read only to place that row.

The row is documentation. It changes no controls, adds no new attack surface and weakens no mitigation, and the cited behaviour cannot be checked against code here. I traced it against the cache threat T-041 (TB-007) and found no regression there. Checkpoint boundary placement may affect which prefixes are donated to the encrypted SSD complete-checkpoint store, but it does not change the cache crypto, the HMAC lookup tags, the 30-minute TTL or the coordinator-authored cacheSalt scoping. T-041's per-donation gating and SEC-035 acceptance are not contradicted by this row. The row makes no claim about security, so no threat-model update is warranted from the supplied evidence.

The actual implementation (the scheduler range-splitting code and its interaction with cacheable-request scoping) is outside the supplied evidence. If the code PR is reviewed, check that demanded checkpoint boundaries still honor the cacheSalt scope and the donation gating. This doc line alone raises no concern.
